title: Heartbreak High
synopsis: You made a map of every romantic and sexual connection at your Sydney high school. It got out. Now the school wants you in 'sexual literacy' — and several relationships, including yours, want a word.

nodes.text: The map, drawn in marker, occupies an entire toilet wall. Lines connect names you barely thought about and names you most certainly did. The principal's heels click down the hallway. You have three minutes.

choices.text: Take photos of the map first
choices.consequence: Document the chaos you made.

choices.text: Try to scrub it before assembly
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Try to scrub it before assembly” back. Damage control shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Quinni sees you with the camera. She doesn't judge. She does, helpfully, point out that you spelled three names wrong. Friendship like Quinni's is rare and you do not deserve it.

choices.text: Apologize to Quinni for involving her
choices.consequence: Friendship over scoops.

choices.text: Recruit Quinni to help you fix it
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Practical first—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Principal Stacy stares at the map for a long minute. Then she looks at you. 'My office,' she says, evenly. 'And bring whichever friend convinced you the marker was washable.'

choices.text: Take Quinni with you
choices.consequence: “Take Quinni with you” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Backup.

choices.text: Go alone — own it
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Solo.

nodes.text: The new mandatory class is called 'SLT' by the school and 'SLuTs' by everyone else. The teacher is well-intentioned and overwhelmed. The class is, of course, the exact people you mapped.

choices.text: Participate honestly
choices.consequence: “Participate honestly” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Lean in.

choices.text: Sit at the back with Quinni and Darren
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Survive.

nodes.text: Malakai, your maybe-boyfriend, finds you at lunch. 'I'm on the map twice,' he says. 'Did you not notice or not care?' You realize you didn't actually know about the second line until you re-read it.

choices.text: Apologize fully
choices.consequence: Own the harm.

choices.text: Explain the map's intent
choices.consequence: Context as defense.

nodes.text: Darren, equal parts dramatic and wise, says, 'You made the map because you wanted everyone to admit they're connected. The school doesn't want them to.' Darren is right, as usual.

choices.text: Lean into Darren's framing
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Politicize it—follows you into whatever comes next.

choices.text: Lean away — you didn't mean it to be political
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is De-escalate.

nodes.text: You and Quinni share a detention with three people you mapped. The conversation, surprisingly, gets honest. You discover the map left out a connection that, in person, is obvious.

choices.text: Add the connection to a mental version
choices.consequence: You commit to “Add the connection to a mental version.” The story records the instinct as “Stay curious” and carries it forward.

choices.text: Decide the map was a bad idea entirely
choices.consequence: You commit to “Decide the map was a bad idea entirely.” The story records the instinct as “Reconsider” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Students stage a walkout — not, technically, because of you. Then it kind of becomes because of you. The local news has a microphone in your face. Principal Stacy has a vein in her forehead.

choices.text: Speak to the news, briefly
choices.consequence: Take responsibility publicly.

choices.text: Walk past the news in solidarity
choices.consequence: Action over interview.

nodes.text: Spider — boy, dumb, mostly — apologizes for the comment that started a fight last week. He is, briefly, a person. You realize the map, accidentally, gave him a way to think about himself.

choices.text: Accept his apology
choices.consequence: “Accept his apology” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Allow change.

choices.text: Tell him to apologize to the actual people he hurt
choices.consequence: You commit to “Tell him to apologize to the actual people he hurt.” The story records the instinct as “Redirect” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Malakai, on a bench by the courts, tells you he doesn't want to be a project. He wants to be a boyfriend. You realize the two are not separable for you yet, and that this is a problem.

choices.text: Choose the boyfriend part for now
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Commit—follows you into whatever comes next.

choices.text: Be honest that you can't yet
choices.consequence: Honesty hurts cleaner.

nodes.text: Quinni, who hates loud places and loud weeks, has had enough. She skips school. You find her at the planetarium. You sit beside her in the dark while a recorded voice describes Saturn.

choices.text: Skip the rest of the week with her
choices.consequence: Friendship over school.

choices.text: Promise to take fewer of her spoons
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Promise to take fewer of her spoons” back. Mindful shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Sasha, who lives on righteous causes, organizes a 'Connection Festival' to claim the map's energy for queer joy. You realize, with a complicated feeling, that the work you started has gotten away from you and become better.

choices.text: Help organize the festival
choices.consequence: Lean into the better version.

choices.text: Step back and let it be theirs
choices.consequence: “Step back and let it be theirs” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Generosity.

nodes.text: Your mom — too cool, too tired — knocks on your door at 11. She heard about the map from another mum. She doesn't yell. She makes tea. She asks if you've been okay, actually, lately.

choices.text: Tell her the truth about the year
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Tell her the truth about the year” back. Adult conversation shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

choices.text: Promise her a longer talk on Saturday
choices.consequence: Schedule the honesty.

nodes.text: Lights strung between the basketball hoops. Music from someone's brother's DJ rig. The map, redrawn by Sasha, is now a giant mural and includes everyone's pronouns and a few jokes only your year understands.

choices.text: Dance, fully, without your phone
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Be present—follows you into whatever comes next.

choices.text: Sit on the bleachers with Quinni and Darren
choices.consequence: “Sit on the bleachers with Quinni and Darren” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Quieter joy.

nodes.text: Reports come out. The school will not, after all, expel you. Principal Stacy writes a note in pencil: 'You have a knack for systems. Use it.' You will, you think, take her advice.

choices.text: Apply for the school newspaper editor role next term
choices.consequence: Use the knack.

choices.text: Take a term off everything official
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Take a term off everything official” back. Recover shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Year twelve begins. Quinni runs for SRC. Darren auditions for a play that is, secretly, also a coming-out. Malakai sends you a letter that is, in handwriting, a real letter. You are, against the odds, hopeful.

choices.text: Throw yourself into year twelve fully
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Commit.

choices.text: Take it one term at a time
choices.consequence: “Take it one term at a time” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Pace yourself.

nodes.text: On the last day of term you and Quinni and Darren and Sasha and Malakai end up at Bondi at sunset for no good reason. Someone has chips. Someone has a bluetooth speaker that only plays one song.

choices.text: Take a group photo for the year
choices.consequence: Preserve the moment.

choices.text: Just live the moment, no photo
choices.consequence: “Just live the moment, no photo” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Be there.

nodes.text: The night your mum and you go to the parent-teacher evening you both pretend to be normal. Mr. Pavlovic says, quietly, that you have a gift for writing. Your mum holds your shoulder. You realize the year is starting in earnest.

choices.text: Take the writing track seriously
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Aim.

choices.text: Keep it just as a hobby
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Quiet.

nodes.text: Sasha announces a second Connection Festival. You all help. The school, having learned, gives them the gym this time. The night is louder, kinder, and full of someone's bluetooth speaker playing exactly one song.

choices.text: Dance for the whole festival
choices.consequence: You commit to “Dance for the whole festival.” The story records the instinct as “Joy” and carries it forward.

choices.text: Sit and watch your people be happy
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Witness.

nodes.text: The final bell of year twelve. The whole map of who-knew-who tilts into the future. You stand in the courtyard one last time and choose what kind of leaving you'll have.

choices.text: Throw yourself into the next year
choices.consequence: “Throw yourself into the next year” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Loud goodbye.

choices.text: Take the slow walk out
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Quiet goodbye.

choices.text: Take one last photo of the gang
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Save it.

nodes.text: You become the editor of the school paper. You write a column called 'Connections.' You graduate with a portfolio that gets you into a journalism program. Years later you make a podcast that is, in a real sense, the map grown up.

You take it term by term and survive year twelve without being a story about year twelve. Quinni helps. Darren makes you laugh. Malakai, eventually, becomes the friend he was supposed to be. You graduate quietly, fully, ready.
The photo lives on your fridge for a decade. Different versions of you pass it. None of them know yet how good a year that was. You do.
